summary: Reproduced the OpenAI HTTP model-validation defect on the prepared source checkout, then added shared explicit-model validation for OpenAI serving handlers and the separate Responses API path. Unknown models now return HTTP 404 with code model_not_found; the served model, omitted compatibility default, and registered base:LoRA form remain accepted.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before real HTTP/engine execution: bogus and served model names both returned 200 on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions; bogus response model fields echoed gpt-nonexistent-999. Raw evidence is under evidence/before/.
Four regression tests plus two subtests passed, covering unknown, served, omitted, explicit default, registered LoRA, missing LoRA, and mismatched-base LoRA cases.
Passing-after real HTTP/engine execution: bogus model names returned 404 model_not_found on both reported endpoints, while served-name requests returned 200. Raw evidence is under evidence/after/.
All applicable repository formatting, lint, safety, and registered-test validation hooks passed.

remaining_limitations: The qualified fixture is a deterministic tiny random Llama and validates transport plus engine execution only; it does not validate Meta-Llama-3.1-8B semantic accuracy or any other model architecture.
Only the assigned single gfx950 GPU was used; distributed and multi-node paths were not exercised.
The Rust model-gateway path was inspected but not changed or runtime-tested because the reproduced defect and correction are in the Python HTTP server path.
The /v1/responses path shares the validation helper and was wired explicitly, but the real-GPU probes targeted the two endpoints named in the report: chat completions and completions.
